Subject: Structured prepay sweep, ramp and true-up — initial proposal

Hi Elena / procurement team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached an initial schedule (v1) that maps a 3-year committed relationship into an annual prepay drawdown mechanism that accommodates a customer ramp. High-level:

- Term: 3 years (annual prepay each anniversary).
- Commit mechanics: Nimbus prepays each year into a dedicated drawdown pool; Redwood performs a monthly sweep that deducts actual usage from the prepaid balance (the "monthly sweep / drawdown").
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 is conservatively set at 60% of forecasted run-rate, Year 2 at 85%, Year 3 at 100% (see tab "Ramp" in the attachment). The annual prepay amounts and month-by-month drawdown percentages are in the spreadsheet.
- Discounts: volume discount tiers applied to committed prepay balance (not to overage): 15% for Year 1 aggregate commit, 20% Year 2, 24% Year 3. Overage beyond prepaid drawdown billed PAYG at list price less 5%.
- True-up: annual true-up at each anniversary. If actual 12-month spend > prepaid amount, Redwood issues an invoice for the shortfall at agreed post-discount rates. If actual < prepaid and unused prepaid balance <= 25% of that year’s prepay, funds carry forward to the next year and expire after 6 months; amounts >25% are eligible for a one-time conversion to a credit at a reduced conversion (75% of unused value) or refund subject to a 90-day processing period and admin fee.

Items we specifically want your feedback on: 1) carry-forward cap (we proposed 25%), 2) true-up cadence (we propose annual), 3) whether overage discount at "list minus 5%" is acceptable, 4) any procurement/PO requirements we should bake into the term sheet.

Attached: 2026-09-15_Redwood-prepay-schedule_v1.xlsx (tabs: Summary, Ramp, MonthlyDrawdown, Pricing).

If the structure looks generally OK I can circulate a one-page term summary for signatures and get legal to prepare a DocuSign-ready term sheet. Would you be available next Wed to finalize?

Best,

Hi Elena — quick replies inline to your questions: 

1) Carry-forward rationale: the 6-month expiry is intended to balance cost predictability for Redwood with flexibility for Nimbus to use credits during a near-term delay. That said, we can be flexible: we can extend carry-forward to 12 months at the following concession — the conversion value on carry-forward >25% will be reduced (from 75% to 65%) and the Year 1 discount would move from 15% to 13%. This is a common trade-off when extending carry-forward windows.

2) Refund policy: refunds are allowed once per contract year, subject to a 90-day processing period. Administrative processing fee is 2% of the refunded amount. Refunds are calculated on the net prepaid amount (post-discount). So if you prepay $1,000,000 at 15% discount, the refund base is the $850,000 net value.

3) Overage pricing: overage pricing applies immediately once the monthly sweep indicates the prepaid balance is exhausted; overage is billed at the next month’s invoice. We offer a safety buffer where if projected monthly usage would exceed the remaining prepaid by >20%, Redwood can notify and temporarily throttle or suggest a top-up to avoid surprise billing.

4) Mid-year ramp adjustments: yes, we can support a formal mid-year ramp amendment. Changes before the mid-year true-up will be applied prospectively. For material increases (>=30%) we require at least 60 days' notice to align capacity.

One other point: if Nimbus wants a staged drawdown option (instead of a single lump-sum annual prepay), we can offer a quarterly staged prepay (four equal payments per year) at the same aggregated discount if PO/payment timing is an issue. Happy to model both in the sheet.

—Rishi

Key changes in v2: 

- Carry-forward: 6-month default; alternate 12-month at concession (see above).
- Refunds: allowed once/year; 90-day processing; 2% admin fee; refunds on net prepaid (post-discount).
- Overage: PAYG at list minus 5% billed monthly once balance exhausted; safety buffer and notification threshold at 20%.
- Staged prepay option: quarterly prepay available at same aggregate discount if procurement timing requires it.
- Early termination: pro-rated refund after two-year mark; if termination in Year 1, refund subject to deduction of a 10% early termination handling fee (documented in the term sheet).

Attached: 2026-09-20_Redwood-term-summary_v2.docx (term summary + short SOW checklist). Please review the two carry-forward options and let me know which one Nimbus prefers. Camila
